title: Order in the Court
subtitle: The hospital needs a sorted patient report
conceptSummary: ORDER BY can sort by multiple columns: ORDER BY col1 DESC, col2 ASC — it sorts by col1 first, then by col2 for ties.

dialogue.text: City Hospital needs a report: all appointments sorted by date (newest first), then by fee (highest first) for same dates.
Multi-column ORDER BY. Comma-separate the columns. First column is primary sort, second breaks ties.

teachMoment.title: Sorting by Multiple Columns
teachMoment.body:
ORDER BY can take multiple columns:

ORDER BY appt_date DESC, fee_paid DESC

This sorts by date first (newest first). If two appointments share a date, the higher fee appears first.

Think of it like sorting a deck: first by suit, then by number within each suit.

task.instruction: Get all completed appointments. Sort by appt_date (newest first), then by fee_paid (highest first).
task.startingQuery:
SELECT appt_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appt_date, fee_paid
FROM appointments
WHERE status = 'completed'
ORDER BY
task.solution: SELECT appt_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appt_date, fee_paid FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' ORDER BY appt_date DESC, fee_paid DESC

hints.text: You need two columns in ORDER BY, separated by a comma.
ORDER BY appt_date DESC, fee_paid DESC
Full: SELECT appt_id, patient_id, doctor_id, appt_date, fee_paid FROM appointments WHERE status = 'completed' ORDER BY appt_date DESC, fee_paid DESC

winDialogue.text: Report sorted! And patient 301 (Alok Tiwari) visited BOTH cardiology AND neurology on the same day. How?
Duplicate patient records. Or someone scheduled him in twice to inflate the billing. More data manipulation!

storyBeat: The data manipulation ring is wider than we thought. It spans pizza orders, cricket stats, metro payments, AND hospital billing. SHADOW42 is not one person — it's an organized network.
